title: Finite-blockade dynamics of a three-qubit ccz gate in neutral-atom arrays
abstract: We present a theoretical study of finite-blockade dynamics in a symmetric three-neutral-atom system, providing a framework for understanding high-fidelity multiqubit quantum operations. The transition from the finite- to the strong-blockade regime is systematically investigated to examine the effects of finite Rydberg blockade. Using a single Gaussian laser pulse, we analyze the complete gate dynamics while explicitly accounting for population leakage into non-computational Rydberg states. By exploiting the permutation symmetry of the system, we construct a symmetry-adapted Hamiltonian that reduces the computational complexity while preserving the exact dynamics. This enables a systematic investigation of the interplay among the Rabi frequency, laser detuning, and Rydberg blockade strength, leading to the identification of optimal operating regimes with high fidelity, fast gate operation, and suppressed leakage. We further quantify the dominant error mechanisms, including phase errors, population leakage, and finite Rydberg-state lifetimes, and evaluate their impact on the gate fidelity. Our results demonstrate experimentally accessible high-fidelity gate operation and provide practical guidelines for multi-qubit quantum computing.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the implementation of a three-qubit CCZ gate in neutral-atom arrays by modeling finite-blockade dynamics. The authors systematically investigate how imperfections, such as finite blockade effects and Rydberg state decay, degrade gate fidelity. They provide optimal operating regimes and error quantification guidelines for realizing high-fidelity quantum gates.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamics of a three-qubit Controlled-Controlled-Z (CCZ) gate implemented using Rydberg blockade in neutral-atom arrays.
main_result: High-fidelity gate operation is achievable by carefully tuning the interplay between the Rabi frequency, detuning, and blockade strength, while also accounting for population leakage and finite Rydberg-state decay.
method: The authors employ a theoretical Hamiltonian approach, utilizing symmetry-adapted bases to reduce computational complexity and analyze the time evolution under both coherent and non-Hermitian (decay) terms.
model_or_system: The system consists of three neutral $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ atoms trapped in optical tweezers, where qubit operations are mediated by Rydberg blockade interactions. The dynamics are modeled by an effective Hamiltonian that includes coupling to non-computational Rydberg states.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($F$), population leakage ($P_1, P_{11}, P_{111}$), and the accumulated CCZ phase ($\phi_{	ext{ccz}}$).
important_parameters: Rabi frequency ($\Omega(t)$), laser detuning ($\Delta$), Rydberg blockade strength ($V$), and decay rate ($\Gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis systematically moves beyond the ideal strong-blockade limit to the finite-blockade regime, and later incorporates decay using a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometric setup and pulse profile, the schematic of the CCZ gate, and plots showing gate error dependence on detuning and interaction strength, including the effect of decay rates.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the system and the CCZ gate mechanism, to analyzing the dynamics in the finite-blockade regime, and finally incorporating decoherence via non-Hermitian decay terms to quantify error sources.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the practical limitations (finite blockade, decay) of implementing multi-qubit gates using neutral atoms, providing concrete guidelines for experimental optimization.

(b) Gaussian pulse Ω(t) used to drive the Rydberg transition from state |1⟩to |r⟩, with a peak Rabi frequency Ω0. (c) Schematic illustration of the closely spaced rydberg energy levels in the n = 70-90 energy levels.

FIG. 2. (Color online) Schematic representation of a three- atom ccz gate, where the computational basis states undergo a conditional z-phase operation, leaving all states unchanged except |111⟩, which acquires a phase of π.

FIG. 3. (Color online) Symmetry-adapted energy-level dia- gram for three neutral atoms. The global laser field couples the symmetric Dicke ladder |111⟩↔|B1⟩↔|B2⟩↔|rrr⟩, while the dark states remain decoupled. The interaction- induced energy shifts of V and 3V for the doubly and triply excited Rydberg states, respectively, detune these states from the laser resonance, resulting in the Rydberg blockade.

FIG. 4. (Color online) Final population revial of the computational manifolds P1, P2, and P3 as a function of the interaction strength (V/Ω0), showing improved revival with increasing interaction strength due to reduced finite-blockade leakage.

FIG. 5. (Color online)(b) Three-qubit conditional phase (Θ3/π) versus (V/Ω0) for ∆/Ω0 = 0.44, 0.47, 0.49 and 0.51. The horizontal dashed line denotes the ideal CCZ phase condition, Θ3 = π. (c) Average CCZ gate fidelity as a function of (V/Ω0) for the same detunings. The fidelity increases with interaction strength, with ∆/Ω0 = 0.45 providing the highest fidelity over the range considered.
